judge_leakage.note: prompt is an f-string; hashed from source text

scoring_constants.date_score: exp(-0.1 * |months between predicted and ground truth|)
scoring_constants.frq_scale: 0-10 per dimension; frq_score = mean(alignment, specificity, novelty, feasibility); FRQ pass = score >= 5.0

partition_rule.main_tables: pre if pub_month < cutoff_month else post (cutoff month counts as POST) — make_latex_tables.py, compare_models.py
partition_rule.gap_and_calibration_tables: post if pub_month > cutoff_month (cutoff month counts as PRE) — filter_ids_by_cutoff in make_web_search_cutoff_table.py
partition_rule.note: These two conventions differ by one month and BOTH are used in the published tables. Each table is reproduced under the convention its own generator used, so every Sonnet 5 row is comparable with the six published rows in that same table.

rejected_sampling_params.temperature: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': "Unsupported value: 'temperature' does not support 0.0 with this model. Only the default (1) value is supported.", 'type': 'invalid_request_error', 'param': 'temperature', 'code': 'unsupported_value'}}

model_under_test.cutoff_caveat: The cutoff falls MID-MONTH. CUSP publication dates are YYYY-MM only, so February 2026 (211 events) cannot be cleanly assigned to either side of it. Post-cutoff is 252 events if February counts as post, 41 if it counts as pre. Tables report both, and a February-excluded variant.

decoding.thinking: adaptive (always on for this model; not configurable off in the way older models were effectively greedy)
decoding.frq_cap_note: 2048 is the value the five OpenAI-family published models ran with. For OpenAI reasoning models max_completion_tokens covers reasoning tokens too: at 384 the model returns EMPTY text on 10/15 FRQ items because ~310 tokens go to reasoning.

unmatchable_parameters.gpt-5.6-sol: cannot be sent — 400 'does not support 0.0 with this model. Only the default (1) value is supported.' reasoning_effort is sent instead, which suppresses the temperature argument.

judge.api_surface: OpenAI Responses API with the web_search tool (eval.LLMClient._call_responses_api)
two_stage_protocol: stage 1: judge_leakage  — contamination audit, web search forced
stage 2: judge_frq_combined — 4-dimension rubric, 0-10 each, frq_score = unweighted mean of the four
judge.probe_error: RateLimitError: Error code: 429 - {'error': {'message': 'Your requests to gpt-5.4-mini for gpt-5.4-mini in eastus have exceeded rate limit.', 'type': 'too_many_requests', 'param': None, 'code': 'rate_limit_exceeded'}}

capture.reasoning_trace_source: The task prompts themselves require a reasoning field in the JSON response ('reasoning': '<1-2 sentence justification>'), and a confidence field. Both are parsed and stored per item. Coverage on the Sonnet 5 full corpus: reasoning 100% of answered items (mean 237-300 chars per task), confidence 99.2-100%. FRQ is free text, stored verbatim (mean 1,046 chars). This is the reasoning record for the benchmark; no separate API thinking trace is used.
capture.api_thinking_traces: Not used. Anthropic adaptive thinking returns EMPTY summarized blocks on these prompts (0 of 32 calls across all four task types produced text at effort=medium), and gpt-5.6-sol exposes no reasoning text via chat completions, only a reasoning-token count, which IS stored.
capture.token_logprobs: Unavailable on BOTH models. gpt-5.6-sol returns HTTP 400 'logprobs is not supported with this model'; Anthropic exposes logprobs on no model. No logprob-based analysis is possible for either, so none is presented.
